_note: Strum patterns as beat grids. Eight slots to a bar, one per eighth note: 1, 1&, 2, 2&, 3, 3&, 4, 4&. Each slot is "D" for a downstrum, "U" for an upstrum, or null for a slot where the hand keeps moving but does not hit the strings.
_theHandKeepsMoving: The null slots are not rests. Justin: 'you should keep your strumming hand moving, even if you don't hit any strings... just like a pendulum.' The arrows on screen show what she hits; the hand does the whole bar either way, and the third pattern does not work at all without it.
_source: justinguitar.com/guitar-lessons/the-strumming-pattern-b1-404 (THE Strumming Pattern — 'Old Faithful'), read 2026-09-13. His three steps are exactly a three-pattern progression: four downs; then up strums on the backbeat after beats 2 and 3; then skip the down on beat 3, keeping the up after it.
_prdDifference: PRD §3.2 writes the middle pattern as D-D-U-U-D-U, which is Old Faithful with a final up strum on 4&. Justin's lesson never mentions a 4& strum — checked, the page does not contain one — so the app teaches his version and 'syncopated' in the PRD is his third step, where the missing downbeat on 3 is the syncopation. If Ash wants the 4& up, it is one null to change in old-faithful below.
_progression: One pattern per week, three weeks minimum on each (PRD §3.2). Repetition is the mechanism, so the app does not offer a way to skip ahead.
